items.followUp: A machine receives 500 J of energy and produces 350 J of useful output. Calculate its efficiency.

rubric.why: Award for defining efficiency as the ratio of useful output to total input.
rubric.description: Defines efficiency as a ratio of useful work/output to input work/energy.
rubric.how: Look for both useful output and total input in the definition.

rubric.why: Award for the correct formula, including conversion to a percentage.
rubric.how: Check that the output-to-input ratio is multiplied by 100.

modelAnswer: Efficiency is the ratio of useful work done by a machine to the total work supplied to it.
Efficiency = (useful work output / total work input) × 100%.

items.followUp: A metal block has a mass of 2 kg and a volume of 0.001 m³. Find its density.

rubric.why: Award for stating that density is mass per unit volume.
rubric.description: Defines density as mass per unit volume.
rubric.how: Look for mass divided by volume in the definition.

rubric.why: Award for the correct SI unit.
rubric.description: Gives the SI unit as kg m⁻³ (kg/m³).
rubric.how: Check that the unit is kilograms per cubic metre.

modelAnswer: Density is the mass per unit volume of a substance.
Its SI unit is kilogram per cubic metre (kg m⁻³).

items.followUp: What is meant by a balanced force?

rubric.why: Award for identifying that a deforming force changes a body's shape or size.
rubric.description: Defines a deforming force as a force that changes the shape or size of a body.
rubric.how: Look for the force causing a change in shape or size.

modelAnswer: A deforming force is a force that changes the shape or size of a body.

items.followUp: State the SI unit of temperature and the temperature of the lower fixed point on the Celsius scale.

rubric.why: Award for describing temperature as indicating how hot or cold a body is.
rubric.description: Defines temperature as the degree of hotness or coldness of a body.
rubric.how: Look for hotness or coldness as the meaning of temperature.

rubric.why: Award for the SI unit kelvin.
rubric.description: Gives kelvin (K) as the SI unit.
rubric.how: Check that the SI unit is kelvin.

modelAnswer: Temperature is the degree of hotness or coldness of a body.
Its SI unit is kelvin (K).

items.followUp: What is meant by the kinetic energy of the molecules of a body?

rubric.why: Award for identifying molecular kinetic energy as part of internal energy.
rubric.description: States that internal energy includes the kinetic energies of the molecules.
rubric.how: Look for the total or sum of molecular kinetic energies.

rubric.why: Award for including molecular potential energy as the other part.
rubric.description: States that internal energy also includes the potential energies of the molecules.
rubric.how: Look for molecular potential energy as well as kinetic energy.

modelAnswer: The internal energy of a body is the sum of the kinetic and potential energies of its molecules.

items.followUp: What are the fixed points used to calibrate a Celsius thermometer, and what are their values?

rubric.why: Award for identifying the lower fixed point and its value.
rubric.description: Defines the lower fixed point as the ice point, 0 °C.
rubric.how: Look for the ice point or freezing/melting point of water at 0 °C.

rubric.why: Award for identifying the upper fixed point and its value.
rubric.description: Defines the upper fixed point as the steam point, 100 °C.
rubric.how: Look for the steam point or boiling point of water at 100 °C.

modelAnswer: The lower fixed point is the temperature of melting ice, 0 °C, at standard atmospheric pressure.
The upper fixed point is the temperature of steam above boiling water, 100 °C, at standard atmospheric pressure.

items.followUp: Using a velocity-time graph, derive the equation v_f² = v_i² + 2as.

rubric.why: Award for setting up the velocity-time graph with the initial and final velocities.
rubric.description: Shows or describes a velocity-time graph with time on the horizontal axis and velocity on the vertical axis, from vᵢ at t = 0 to v_f at time t.
rubric.how: Check that the graph description identifies the axes and the initial and final velocity points.

rubric.why: Award for obtaining acceleration as the slope of the graph.
rubric.description: Uses the slope of the velocity-time graph to write a = (v_f − vᵢ)/t.
rubric.how: Look for acceleration expressed as change in velocity divided by time.

rubric.why: Award for relating displacement to the area under the velocity-time graph.
rubric.description: Uses the trapezium area to obtain s = ½(vᵢ + v_f)t.
rubric.how: Check for the correct average-velocity displacement relation from the graph.

rubric.why: Award for the required final equation.
rubric.description: Rearranges the acceleration relation to derive v_f = vᵢ + at.
rubric.how: Check that the final equation has the correct signs and terms.

modelAnswer: Draw a velocity-time graph with time t on the horizontal axis and velocity v on the vertical axis.
Mark the initial velocity vᵢ at t = 0 and the final velocity v_f at time t.
The slope of the graph gives acceleration: a = (v_f − vᵢ) / t.
Rearranging: v_f − vᵢ = at.
Therefore, v_f = vᵢ + at.

items.followUp: A 0.20 kg stone is rotated in a circle of radius 0.80 m at a speed of 4 m s⁻¹. Find the tension in the string.

rubric.why: Award for correctly converting the mass to SI units and identifying the given quantities.
rubric.description: Writes the given data in SI units: m = 0.1 kg, r = 1 m, v = 5 m s⁻¹.
rubric.how: Check that the mass is converted from 100 g to 0.1 kg and the radius and speed are stated.

rubric.why: Award for the centripetal-force relation that gives the string tension.
rubric.how: Look for mass multiplied by speed squared and divided by radius.

rubric.why: Award for substituting the SI values and evaluating the expression correctly.
rubric.description: Substitutes T = (0.1 kg × (5 m s⁻¹)²) / 1 m and obtains 2.5 kg m s⁻².
rubric.how: Check for the numerical substitution with units and the correct evaluation.

rubric.why: Award for the final tension with its correct unit.
rubric.how: Check that the final answer is 2.5 newtons.

modelAnswer: Given: m = 100 g = 0.1 kg, r = 1 m, v = 5 m s⁻¹.
The tension supplies the centripetal force: T = mv² / r.
T = 2.5 kg m s⁻².
